newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end higher for eighth day in row.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end higher for eighth day in row.

text.p: Sri lankan share prices ended higher for the eighth consecutive day on Wednesday on bargain hunting by retail investors, but some brokers said they were not optimistic about the future of the bourse.

The all share index closed 4.4 points higher at 589.7, driven by retail investors vying to capitalise on current low prices in the market, brokers said. The index has risen 4.9 percent in the past two weeks.
"Retailers feel prices are at their lowest and cannot go down any further," a broker for Asia Stock Brokers said. "They are buying small quantities and pushing up stocks by small margins."

Gains outnumbered declines by 40 to four. Commercial Bank rights shares rose four rupees to 22 rupees and Lanka Wall Tile three to 31 rupees. Turnover was a thin 13.2 million rupees, down from Monday's 15 million rupees.
Some brokers doubted the current uptrend would continue in the future.
"The economic fundamentals don't support this retail buying trend. Conditions which pushed the market down still prevail. So you wonder how long this is going to last," the Asia broker said.
